what_it_does: Provides antioxidant support and helps calm the look of stressed skin.
summary_short: EGCG is a green tea polyphenol used mainly for antioxidant and soothing support. It may help reduce the look of redness, excess oil, and environmental stress, though results depend heavily on formula stability and concentration.
summary_long:
**Epigallocatechin Gallate (EGCG)** is one of the best-known antioxidant compounds found in green tea. In skincare, it is used to help neutralize free radicals triggered by UV exposure, pollution, and other environmental stressors. This does not replace sunscreen, but it can complement a daily protective routine.

EGCG is also studied for its soothing and oil-balancing potential. Limited clinical and lab evidence suggests it may help calm visible redness, support blemish-prone skin, and reduce the appearance of excess sebum. These effects are promising, but topical results can vary because EGCG is sensitive to light, oxygen, heat, and formula pH.

In products, EGCG may appear as a purified ingredient or as part of green tea extract. Leave-on formulas often use low percentages, while green tea extracts vary widely in EGCG content, so the ingredient list alone does not tell you how much active EGCG is present.

EGCG is generally well tolerated, especially in moisturizers and serums. Sensitive skin may still react to concentrated green tea extracts, alcohol-heavy formulas, fragrance, or acidic systems, so patch testing is reasonable if your skin is reactive.

It pairs well with sunscreen, niacinamide, panthenol, hyaluronic acid, vitamin E, and other calming antioxidants. It may be less reliable in poorly packaged products, especially clear jars or formulas exposed often to air and light.
quick_facts: May support oily or blemish-prone skin
